recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing the original ignore-id sentence would conflict with later published decisions; any future behavior change should be handled under a newer finalized conditional-update tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-13989 was a Published FHIR-I STU3 change request, resolved Persuasive, asking whether a submitted resource may include Resource.id during conditional update. The original resolution allowed an id in the instance and said the server should ignore it by referring to create/id-handling guidance.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit 91be5c2880262ecd2d4ad09ca259612955bcf24d, matching Jira comment svn revision 14199. That commit added a conditional update paragraph in source/http.html saying the resource MAY contain an id, does not need to, and that a supplied id is ignored.
additional_context: source/http.html is in the current build via publish.ini. Later finalized same-section issues superseded the blanket ignore-id wording: FHIR-17906 introduced Resource.id-sensitive conditional update outcomes, FHIR-20390 clarified that the outcomes refer to Resource.id and also requested removal of the ignore sentence, FHIR-26688 specifically resolved that the ignore-id sentence was mistaken and should be removed, and FHIR-36859 further split the no-match Resource.id-provided case based on whether that id already exists.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/http.html states that a conditional update resource MAY contain an id but does not need to, and the outcome list now defines the later approved handling for absent, matching, mismatching, new, and already-existing Resource.id cases.
